info.name: BuildBaseKit AuthKit-Lite API — Human Test Suite
info.description:
# AuthKit-Lite API — Human Test Suite

Use this collection in either of two ways:

## Run every automatable API as one workflow

1. Start AuthKit-Lite with the `dev` profile and a MySQL database.
2. Confirm `baseUrl` and the seeded admin credentials in the collection Variables tab.
3. Select **01 — Guided Full API Test** and click **Run**.
4. Keep the saved request order. The first request creates a fresh test identity and clears old runtime tokens.
5. Review the test summary. The guided folder covers operations, registration, password login, JWT authorization, refresh rotation and replay rejection, logout, admin authorization, CSRF, CORS, and WebAuthn option endpoints.

## Run one API at a time

Open any request and read its **Docs** description. Each request states its prerequisites, expected result, and variables it saves. For protected endpoints, run the relevant login request first or paste a token into the collection Variables tab.

## Generated and saved values

With `autoGenerateUser=true`, the collection creates a unique `username` and `email`. Login, refresh, admin login, and CSRF requests automatically save their returned values. Runtime token variables intentionally start empty.

## Browser-only passkey operations

The **02 — Browser Passkey Templates** folder contains every remaining WebAuthn endpoint. These templates are skipped unless `runBrowserRequests=true`, because Postman cannot call `navigator.credentials.create()` or `navigator.credentials.get()`. Paste authenticator output captured by a browser before sending them.

The collection uses safe local demo values only. Do not store production passwords, secrets, access tokens, or refresh tokens in a shared collection.

item.name: 00 — Read Me First
item.description:
# Quick start

## Combined test

Select **01 — Guided Full API Test**, click **Run**, keep the displayed order, and start the run. Use a fresh or reusable local database; unique normal-user credentials are generated for every run.

The administrator requests expect the development seed account. Start the application with:

```bash
./mvnw spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=dev
```

## Individual API test

1. Open a request.
2. Read its Docs panel.
3. Satisfy the listed prerequisite request or enter the needed collection variable.
4. Click **Send**.

Typical setup requests:

- Normal-user JWT: **02 · Registration & Password Login → Login normal user and save tokens**
- Administrator JWT: **05 · Administrator APIs → Login administrator and save tokens**
- WebAuthn CSRF/session: **06 · WebAuthn Options, CSRF & CORS → Obtain WebAuthn CSRF token and cookie**

## Reset

Run **01 · Start a new test run** to create another unique normal user and clear saved runtime values. Postman's cookie jar should remain enabled for WebAuthn requests.

item.name: 01 — Guided Full API Test
item.description:
Run this folder to execute all Postman-compatible APIs as one ordered workflow.

The first request resets generated identity and runtime variables. Login, refresh, admin login, and CSRF requests chain their output automatically. Negative tests are intentionally included and pass only when the API returns the documented rejection status.

You can also expand this folder and send any request individually; each request documents its prerequisites.

item.name: 01 · Start & Operational Endpoints

request.description:
### Purpose

Starts a clean guided run and verifies actuator discovery.

### Prerequisites

None. The application must be running.

### Expected result

200 JSON containing links to exposed actuator endpoints.

### Variables saved

Generates runId/username/email and clears runtime tokens.

exec: throw new Error('Set username and email, or set autoGenerateUser=true.');
pm.test("Health and info links exist", () => { const links=pm.response.json()._links; pm.expect(links.health.href).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(links.info.href).to.be.a("string"); });

item.name: 04 · Refresh Rotation & User Logout
01 · Rotate refresh token and save new tokens

request.description:
### Purpose

Consumes the current refresh token and atomically issues a new access/refresh pair.

### Prerequisites

refreshToken populated by normal-user login.

### Expected result

200 with rotated tokens.

### Variables saved

oldRefreshToken, accessToken, and refreshToken.

### Purpose

Attempts to reuse the consumed refresh token.

### Prerequisites

Rotate refresh token must have run.

### Expected result

401 Unauthorized.

### Variables saved

Nothing.

### Purpose

Confirms the access token returned by refresh authenticates successfully.

### Prerequisites

Rotate refresh token must have run.

### Expected result

200 current-user profile.

### Variables saved

Nothing.

### Purpose

Revokes the current normal-user refresh token. The access token authenticates the logout request.

### Prerequisites

Current accessToken and refreshToken.

### Expected result

200 logout confirmation.

### Variables saved

Nothing.

### Purpose

Confirms the refresh token revoked during logout cannot be reused.

### Prerequisites

Logout current refresh token must have run.

### Expected result

401 Unauthorized.

### Variables saved

Nothing.

item.description:
Runs the full refresh-token lifecycle: rotate, reject replay, use the new access token, logout, and reject the revoked refresh token.

**Prerequisite:** Normal-user login must have saved `accessToken` and `refreshToken`. Run this folder in order.

item.name: 06 · WebAuthn Options, CSRF & CORS
01 · Obtain WebAuthn CSRF token and cookie

request.description:
### Purpose

Creates/reuses a WebAuthn session and obtains the CSRF token required by stateful WebAuthn POST/DELETE requests.

### Prerequisites

Postman cookie jar enabled.

### Expected result

200 JSON token plus XSRF-TOKEN Set-Cookie header.

### Variables saved

csrfToken; matching cookies remain in Postman's cookie jar.

### Purpose

Requests WebAuthn assertion options for the configured username.

### Prerequisites

Run Obtain WebAuthn CSRF token first in the same Postman session.

### Expected result

200 WebAuthn PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions JSON.

### Variables saved

Session challenge is retained server-side.

### Purpose

Requests WebAuthn registration options for the JWT-authenticated administrator used by the guided workflow. The endpoint behaves identically for any authenticated credential owner.

### Prerequisites

adminAccessToken plus csrfToken and matching session cookie. For individual normal-user testing, change Authorization to use {{accessToken}}.

### Expected result

200 WebAuthn PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions JSON.

### Variables saved

Session challenge is retained for browser enrollment.

### Purpose

Proves WebAuthn POST endpoints reject a missing CSRF header.

### Prerequisites

None; any retained cookie is acceptable.

### Expected result

403 Forbidden.

### Variables saved

Nothing.

Tests all WebAuthn server operations that do not require an authenticator: CSRF exchange, authentication options, registration options, missing-CSRF rejection, and CORS.

item.name: 02 — Browser Passkey Templates (Manual)
item.description:
These requests complete the API inventory but require data created by a real browser authenticator.

## Before sending

1. Complete normal-user registration and login.
2. Obtain WebAuthn CSRF/session state.
3. Request registration or authentication options.
4. Use those options with `navigator.credentials.create()` or `navigator.credentials.get()` in a browser on an allowed origin.
5. Serialize the browser credential to JSON and paste it into the matching collection variable.
6. Set `runBrowserRequests=true`.
7. Send only the relevant request.

Leave `runBrowserRequests=false` for normal guided or whole-collection runs; these requests will be reported as skipped rather than sending empty authenticator payloads.

exec: console.log('Skipped: set runBrowserRequests=true after pasting real browser authenticator output.');

request.description:
### Purpose

Submits the browser-created attestation and enrolls a passkey for the authenticated normal user.

### Prerequisites

Normal-user accessToken, matching WebAuthn CSRF/session, registration options, real navigator.credentials.create() output in webauthnRegistrationResponse, and runBrowserRequests=true.

### Expected result

200 successful registration response. Then list passkeys to obtain the stored credential identifier.

### Variables saved

Nothing automatically; copy the credential ID returned by the passkey-list request into credentialId.

item.name: 02 · Complete passkey authentication and save tokens

exec: console.log('Skipped: set runBrowserRequests=true after pasting real browser authenticator output.');

request.description:
### Purpose

Submits a browser-created passkey assertion. On success, AuthKit returns its normal JWT and refresh-token response.

### Prerequisites

Matching authentication-options session and CSRF token, real navigator.credentials.get() output in webauthnAuthenticationResponse, and runBrowserRequests=true.

### Expected result

200 with accessToken and refreshToken.

### Variables saved

accessToken and refreshToken.

exec: console.log('Skipped: set runBrowserRequests=true after pasting real browser authenticator output.');

request.description:
### Purpose

Deletes an enrolled passkey through Spring Security's ownership-checked endpoint.

### Prerequisites

Authenticated owner accessToken, matching CSRF/session state, credentialId from passkey list, and runBrowserRequests=true.

### Expected result

200 when the credential exists and belongs to the authenticated user.

### Variables saved

Nothing.
